# Overview

This document fits a hierarchical Bayesian model to USA National
Phenology Network (USA-NPN) flowering observations for red maple (*Acer
rubrum*). Each record is a yes/no (`phenophase_status` = 1/0) answer to
whether the individual plant was flowering on a given day of year.
"Uncertain" records (`phenophase_status == -1`) carry no reliable
presence/absence signal and are removed during data preparation.

The probability that an individual is flowering on a given day is
described by a **double-logistic curve**: a rising edge (onset) followed
by a falling edge (offset), giving a single seasonal "bump." Individual
plants differ in *when* they flower and *how much* they flower, so
several curve parameters are treated as random effects, with the timing
parameters additionally allowed to vary along a latitudinal gradient.

# Setup and data preparation

We read the *Acer rubrum* flower files, drop uncertain records, derive
the observation year, and fold day 366 into day 365. A random subset of
50 individuals is selected for model development.

```{r}
#| label: data-prep
library(tidyverse)

# ---- user choices ----
phenophase <- "flower" # "flower" or "leaf"
genus <- "Acer" # genus folder name
species <- "rubrum" # species epithet, or NA to keep all species in the genus

# ---- build path and read ----
dir_path <- file.path("alldata/input/NPN", phenophase, genus)
ls_files <- list.files(dir_path, full.names = TRUE)

df_npn_all <- read_csv(ls_files) |>
  drop_na(species) |>
  filter(species == !!species) |>
  filter(phenophase_status != -1) |>
  mutate(year = lubridate::year(observation_date)) |>
  select(site_id, latitude, longitude, individual_id, year, day_of_year, phenophase_status) |>
  mutate(day_of_year = case_when(
    day_of_year == 366 ~ 365,
    TRUE ~ day_of_year
  ))

set.seed <- 42
v_id <- df_npn_all$individual_id |>
  unique() |>
  sample(50)

df_npn <- df_npn_all |>
  filter(individual_id %in% v_id)

df_npn |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_point(aes(x = day_of_year, y = phenophase_status, col = as.factor(individual_id)), alpha = 0.5, show.legend = F) +
  facet_wrap(. ~ individual_id)
```

# The double-logistic function

A standalone version of the double-logistic function, used here to
visualize the shape of the curve across a full year.

```{r}
#| label: double-logistic-fn
# Double logistic function

double_logistics <- function(d,
                             m1 = 0,
                             m2 = 1,
                             m3 = 100,
                             m4 = 10,
                             m5 = 160,
                             m6 = 20,
                             m7 = 0,
                             sd = 0.02) {
  v <- m1 + (m2 - m7 * d) * (1 / (1 + exp((m3 - d) / m4)) - 1 / (1 + exp((m5 - d) / m6))) + rnorm(1, 0, sd)

  return(v)
}

df <- data.frame(
  d = 1:365
) |>
  mutate(y = double_logistics(d, sd = 0))

df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = d, y = y)) +
  geom_point()
```

# Model structure {#model-structure}

## Observation model

For observation $i$ on individual $j$ at day-of-year $d_i$, the
flowering status is Bernoulli with probability $p_i$:

$$y_i \sim \text{Bernoulli}(p_i)$$

The probability follows a double-logistic curve scaled by an
individual-specific amplitude $m_2^{(j)}$:

$$p_i = m_2^{(j)} \left[
\frac{1}{1 + \exp\!\big((m_3^{(j)} - d_i)/m_4\big)}
-
\frac{1}{1 + \exp\!\big((m_5^{(j)} - d_i)/m_6\big)}
\right]$$

where

- $m_2^{(j)} \in (0,1)$ — peak flowering probability (amplitude) for
  individual $j$,
- $m_3^{(j)}$ — rising-edge midpoint (onset day) for individual $j$,
- $m_5^{(j)}$ — falling-edge midpoint (offset day) for individual $j$,
- $m_4, m_6$ — shared rising / falling steepness parameters.

## Onset and peak width

To guarantee that offset occurs after onset ($m_5^{(j)} > m_3^{(j)}$),
the model parameterizes the **peak width**
$w^{(j)} = m_5^{(j)} - m_3^{(j)} > 0$ rather than $m_5$ directly:

$$m_5^{(j)} = m_3^{(j)} + w^{(j)}$$

Both the onset $m_3^{(j)}$ and the width $w^{(j)}$ are given
individual-level distributions whose means depend linearly on (centered)
latitude $\tilde{\ell}_j = \ell_j - \bar{\ell}$:

$$m_3^{(j)} \sim \mathcal{N}\!\big(a_{m_3} + b_{m_3}\,\tilde{\ell}_j,\; \sigma_{m_3}\big)$$

$$w^{(j)} \sim \mathcal{N}^{+}\!\big(a_{w} + b_{w}\,\tilde{\ell}_j,\; \sigma_{w}\big)$$

where $\mathcal{N}^{+}$ denotes a normal truncated to be positive. The
slopes $b_{m_3}$ and $b_{w}$ capture how flowering onset and duration
shift with latitude.

## Amplitude

The amplitude varies by individual but **not** by latitude. It is
modeled on the logit scale so that the transformed value stays within
$(0,1)$:

$$\text{logit}\,m_2^{(j)} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_{m_2}, \sigma_{m_2}),
\qquad
m_2^{(j)} = \frac{1}{1 + \exp(-\text{logit}\,m_2^{(j)})}$$

## Priors

$$m_4, m_6 \sim \text{Uniform}(1, 60), \quad
a_{m_3} \sim \text{Uniform}(1, 365), \quad
a_{w} \sim \text{Uniform}(1, 300),$$

$$b_{m_3}, b_{w} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 10), \qquad
\mu_{m_2} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 2),$$

$$\sigma_{m_3}, \sigma_{w} \sim \mathcal{N}^{+}(0, 5), \qquad
\sigma_{m_2} \sim \mathcal{N}^{+}(0, 1),$$

where $\mathcal{N}^{+}$ denotes a half-normal (normal truncated to the
positive half-line).

# Building the NIMBLE model

The model code below encodes the structure described in [Model
structure](#model-structure): shared steepness, latitudinal gradients on
onset and width, an individual-level logit-scale amplitude, and the
Bernoulli likelihood.

```{r}
#| label: nimble-code
library(nimble)

code <- nimbleCode({
  # shared steepness
  m4 ~ dunif(1, 60)
  m6 ~ dunif(1, 60)

  # ---- latitudinal gradient on rising edge m3 ----
  a_m3 ~ dunif(1, 365)
  b_m3 ~ dnorm(0, sd = 10)
  sd_m3 ~ T(dnorm(0, sd = 5), 0, )

  # ---- latitudinal gradient on peak width ----
  a_w ~ dunif(1, 300)
  b_w ~ dnorm(0, sd = 10)
  sd_w ~ T(dnorm(0, sd = 5), 0, )

  # ---- individual amplitude m2 (logit scale, no latitude) ----
  mu_m2 ~ dnorm(0, sd = 2) # population mean on logit scale
  sd_m2 ~ T(dnorm(0, sd = 1), 0, ) # between-individual SD on logit scale

  for (j in 1:Nind) {
    mu3[j] <- a_m3 + b_m3 * lat_c[j]
    m3[j] ~ dnorm(mu3[j], sd = sd_m3)

    muw[j] <- a_w + b_w * lat_c[j]
    width[j] ~ T(dnorm(muw[j], sd = sd_w), 0, )
    m5[j] <- m3[j] + width[j]

    logit_m2[j] ~ dnorm(mu_m2, sd = sd_m2)
    m2[j] <- 1 / (1 + exp(-logit_m2[j])) # in (0,1)
  }

  for (i in 1:N) {
    p[i] <- m2[ind[i]] * (1 / (1 + exp((m3[ind[i]] - doy[i]) / m4)) -
      1 / (1 + exp((m5[ind[i]] - doy[i]) / m6)))
    y[i] ~ dbern(p[i])
  }
})
```

We map individuals to a consecutive integer index, build one centered
latitude value per individual, and assemble the data and constants for
NIMBLE.

```{r}
#| label: nimble-prep

df_npn <- df_npn |>
  arrange(individual_id) |>
  mutate(ind = as.integer(factor(individual_id)))

# one latitude per individual (centered)
ind_lat <- df_npn |>
  distinct(ind, latitude) |>
  arrange(ind) |>
  pull(latitude)
lat_c <- ind_lat - mean(ind_lat)

dat <- list(
  y   = df_npn$phenophase_status,
  doy = df_npn$day_of_year
)
const <- list(
  N     = nrow(df_npn),
  Nind  = max(df_npn$ind),
  ind   = df_npn$ind,
  lat_c = lat_c
)
```

Initial values for all stochastic nodes:

```{r}
#| label: nimble-inits
inits <- list(
  m4 = 10, m6 = 20,
  a_m3 = 100, b_m3 = 0, sd_m3 = 10,
  a_w = 10, b_w = 0, sd_w = 10,
  mu_m2 = 0, sd_m2 = 1,
  m3 = rep(100, const$Nind),
  width = rep(160, const$Nind),
  logit_m2 = rep(0, const$Nind)
)
```

# Fitting

We build and compile the model and MCMC, then run two chains. The
`Sys.time()` calls bracket the build/compile and sampling stages so
their costs can be inspected separately.

```{r}
#| label: nimble-run
t1 <- Sys.time()
model <- nimbleModel(code, constants = const, data = dat, inits = inits)
cmodel <- compileNimble(model)

conf <- configureMCMC(model,
  monitors = c(
    "a_m3", "b_m3", "sd_m3", "a_w", "b_w", "sd_w",
    "m4", "m6", "mu_m2", "sd_m2", "m3", "m5", "m2"
  )
)
mcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
cmcmc <- compileNimble(mcmc, project = model)
t2 <- Sys.time()
t2 - t1

samples <- runMCMC(cmcmc,
  niter = 10000, nburnin = 2000,
  thin = 5, nchains = 2, samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE
)

t3 <- Sys.time()
t3 - t2

# summary(samples)
```

# Diagnostics

Trace plots and posterior densities for the population-level parameters,
with the two chains overlaid. For the slope parameters `b_m3` and `b_w`,
the dashed line at zero marks "no latitudinal effect."

```{r}
#| label: mcmc-tidy
# samples is a coda mcmc.list -> bind with a chain id
df_MCMC <- purrr::imap_dfr(samples, function(chain, ci) {
  as.data.frame(chain) |>
    mutate(n = row_number(), chain = factor(ci))
}) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(n, chain), names_to = "param", values_to = "value")

# population-level params, in a sensible order
pop_params <- c(
  "a_m3", "b_m3", "sd_m3", "a_w", "b_w", "sd_w",
  "m4", "m6", "mu_m2", "sd_m2"
)

df_pop <- df_MCMC |>
  filter(param %in% pop_params) |>
  mutate(param = factor(param, levels = pop_params))
```

```{r}
#| label: trace-plots
# ---- trace plots ----
p_MCMC <- df_pop |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_line(aes(x = n, y = value, color = chain), linewidth = 0.3) +
  ggthemes::theme_few() +
  facet_wrap(. ~ param, scales = "free_y") +
  tagger::tag_facets(tag_suffix = "", tag_levels = "A") +
  theme(
    tagger.panel.tag.background = element_rect(fill = alpha("white", 0.5)),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
p_MCMC
```

```{r}
#| label: posterior-densities
# ---- posterior densities ----
p_posterior <- df_pop |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_density(aes(x = value, color = chain)) +
  ggthemes::theme_few() +
  facet_wrap(. ~ param, scales = "free") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, col = "red", lty = 2) +
  tagger::tag_facets(tag_suffix = "", tag_levels = "A") +
  theme(
    tagger.panel.tag.background = element_rect(fill = alpha("white", 0.5)),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
p_posterior
```

# Posterior predictive check

For each individual we evaluate the fitted double-logistic probability
across a dense day-of-year grid using that individual's posterior draws
of $m_2$, $m_3$, $m_5$ and the shared $m_4$, $m_6$. The median curve and
95% credible band are overlaid on the observed flowering points.

```{r}
#| label: pp-setup
# --- 0. samples as a matrix (combine chains) ---
sm <- as.matrix(samples) # rows = draws, cols = parameters

# --- 1. map the individuals you want to their model index `ind` ---
# (must use the SAME factor levels you built `ind` from)
ind_map <- df_npn |>
  distinct(individual_id, ind)

v_ind <- ind_map |>
  filter(individual_id %in% v_id) |>
  arrange(individual_id)

# --- 2. dense doy grid ---
doy_grid <- 1:365

# --- 3. the same curve as in the model ---
dl_p <- function(doy, m2, m3, m5, m4, m6) {
  p <- m2 * (1 / (1 + exp((m3 - doy) / m4)) - 1 / (1 + exp((m5 - doy) / m6)))
}


# --- 4. for each requested individual, build posterior predictive p(doy) ---
pp <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(v_ind)), function(r) {
  j <- v_ind$ind[r]
  id <- v_ind$individual_id[r]

  m3_draws <- sm[, paste0("m3[", j, "]")]
  m5_draws <- sm[, paste0("m5[", j, "]")]
  m4_draws <- sm[, "m4"]
  m6_draws <- sm[, "m6"]
  m2_draws <- sm[, paste0("m2[", j, "]")]

  # matrix: rows = draws, cols = doy
  P <- sapply(doy_grid, function(d) {
    dl_p(d, m2_draws, m3_draws, m5_draws, m4_draws, m6_draws)
  })

  data.frame(
    individual_id = id,
    day_of_year = doy_grid,
    med = apply(P, 2, median),
    lower = apply(P, 2, quantile, 0.025),
    upper = apply(P, 2, quantile, 0.975)
  )
}) |> bind_rows()
```

```{r}
#| label: pp-plot
# --- 5. plot: observed points + posterior predictive band ---
df_npn |>
  filter(individual_id %in% v_id) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = pp,
    aes(x = day_of_year, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = pp,
    aes(x = day_of_year, y = med),
    color = "black", linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(
      x = day_of_year, y = phenophase_status,
      col = as.factor(individual_id)
    ),
    alpha = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(. ~ individual_id) +
  labs(
    y = "phenophase status / P(status = 1)",
    x = "day of year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
